<subject>Re: May 3 Farmer Engagement Briefing Prep</subject>
<body>
Thanks Thomas. We shall make the additions you noted below. AgriAlliance (Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on smallholder integration for the farming cooperatives. I agree with you that the mass-market procurement parties should also include complementary testimony. Although we discussed this earlier, I did not receive any firm commitments from the procurement folks that they would sponsor such testimony – it may be an oversight on my part. Nonetheless, procurement testimony by those in the sector should include a discussion of the benefits from GreenHarvest, CropLink, FPC, FarmStack and the others. Might I suggest that AgriIndia, as a large bulk procurer itself, coordinate this effort with the other farm partnership groups?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month. We will need to make some time available during late May for practice panels (assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice cross-examination. At the same time, we also need to start thinking about direct cross-examination of the SCGC/FarmerFront parties (again, assuming we decide to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement). There is merit to cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very well thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent with the AgriTrust's most promising options. On the other hand, there is merit to limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will use the witness box to grandstand. It's something to think about.
</body>

Matthew:

Thanks for your memo. Let me add the following comments. There should be a chapter on the procurement settlement with the key parties listed. Rachit Dave and Tanish should be added to the chapter on impact on commodity yield projections. The AgriVision section where you list AgriMax and CropOne was, I believe, originally supposed to include program benefits for the core aggregators as well, and you should add AgriIndia to the list for that Chapter. Let me know if you concur with my recollection. Thanks, Naksh Dube
